disease_label_per_paper: Atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome after childbirth
presentation_summary: A 33-year-old woman was referred to nephrology 18 days after cesarean delivery of twins with rising creatinine after major postpartum bleeding/surgery.
She had no underlying disease, medication history, family history of renal impairment, recent diarrhea, or neurologic symptoms.
Referral labs showed WBC 8800/uL, hemoglobin 7.7 g/dL, platelets 68000/uL, BUN 33.2 mg/dL, creatinine 2.46 mg/dL, LDH 3958 U/L, and fragmented RBCs on smear.
No enterohemorrhagic E. coli was detected in stool, ADAMTS13 activity was 60%, and renal biopsy was consistent with thrombotic microangiopathy.

Hemodialysis and fresh frozen plasma were given with three dialysis sessions; labs improved and follow-up showed no recurrence. Genetic profiling later showed CFHR4 I536R and CFHR3-CFHR1 copy number gain.
